name: One game, and what it says about itself
description: Everything a page needs about one game that is not a standing. `about` and `limits` are the CARTRIDGE'S OWN COPY out of its manifest -- `limits.boards` being what a season's upload may be -- so a second game is a registration and not a web deploy; a cartridge that ships no `about` gets null and the page drops the section. `weight_classes` is the season's size caps, ordered by cap -- the order admission classifies in. There is no compute cap to join to: a class is its byte limit. The boards a season plays are its own, summarised in `season.maps` and listed at GET .../seasons/{slug}/maps.

tasks.name: Query
tasks.description: THE EFFECTIVE LIMITS, not the cartridge's. A season may override turn_ms and max_turns (its `execution` rules block), and this is the route the site prints them from -- so serving g.manifest -> 'limits' raw would tell a competitor a turn budget the ladder does not play by, which is the exact class of failure the claim's contract exists to delete, reintroduced on the public API. Coalesced the same way the claim coalesces it, from the CURRENT season, because that is the one a reader is about to enter.
